touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.

The node schema (Akien, Q#108, 2026-11-14: CC's proposal, which he approved, plus his flexible metadata field). WHY: nodes have to be really fast, and row ids are fastest; a payload can be anything, so a node points into blobs and lists.

ADDRESS: every reference is one 64-bit integer, the top 16 bits a table tag and the low 48 a row. A list of addresses can name nodes, blobs, leaves in any tree, lists and links. Every pointer is a direct row fetch, and a new kind of thing is a new tag, not a schema change.

nodes (the one long list): row, gen, state (VOID|NOTCACHED|DATA), kind (the payload type), payload (inline when small), blob (an address, when large), meta (flexible json), out (a list address), in (a list address), seq (a change counter for the sync).
lists: row, gen, state, owner, items (bigint[] of addresses), and optional weights (real[], parallel). A long list chains to a next chunk.
links: row, gen, a, b, weight, traversals. One row per link; both endpoints' lists hold its address, so a link is bidirectional and its weight has one home.
blobs: row, gen, state, kind (json|csv|text|bytes|vector...), bytes. Several blobs are a list of blob addresses.

trees: leaf tables keep their shape and weights. A leaf points at a node address, and the node's in list holds the leaf's address back. So each leaf table gains an additive row bigint column and keeps leaf_id, and its table tag is assigned at its birth from a tag registry the home librarian holds (0x0100 upward, synced like nodes); tags.json pins only the core four (CC, a mechanism under Q#108, 2026-11-14).
gen: a reference carries (row, gen). After a VOID row is reused, a mismatch reads loud as gone, never as wrong data.
